issue: M14 — pin the C grammar, whose bytes were unpinned and whose origin was not re-derivable offline
question: Is wasm/tree-sitter-c.wasm a build of the repository's PATCHED vendored source, or a pristine upstream build predating the patch? Everything this lane measures is a measurement of a parse from those bytes.

reproduction.pristineSource: npm pack tree-sitter-c@0.24.1 — the tarball's own published wasm
reproduction.note: Bytes are NOT expected to match: a wasm build carries its emscripten version, compiler flags and section order, so two builds of one grammar differ in sha256. The claim being proven is surface and behaviour identity, which is what the pin verifier measures.

sourceVsWasm.measuredBy: script/m14/verify-grammar-pins.ts sourceVsWasmFor() — the gate's own function, called with this lane's real decision
sourceVsWasm.note: The offline statement that the committed bytes ARE a build of the committed source: every name the vendored src/node-types.json declares exists in the wired wasm, and every wasm-named type is declared by the source. Re-measured on every pin-verifier run. Supertypes are counted separately and are hidden by design.

constructs.label: #if __has_include(<vector>)
constructs.note: #743b: the patch's subject. `<vector>` is not a preproc expression upstream — `<` would have to be a binary operator with a missing left operand.

constructs.label: #if __has_include("meta")
constructs.note: #743b: the quoted spelling of the same shape.

constructs.label: #if FMT_HAS_INCLUDE(<string_view>)
constructs.note: #743b: the wrapper form real headers use.

constructs.label: #if A < B && C > D
constructs.note: THE RISK the patch must not create: `<` stays the comparison operator outside an argument position. The vendored comment says this was pinned clean before the change and must stay clean.

constructs.label: #if MAX(A < B, C < D)
constructs.note: the same risk with a parenthesised comparison, which is the shape most likely to be captured by a header-name token.

constructs.label: struct s { redisAtomic long long x; };
constructs.note: #743: a macro-prefixed type specifier, the reason `macro_prefixed_type_specifier` is a visible node.

constructs.label: #include <stdio.h>
constructs.note: CONTROL: the ordinary include, which every candidate parses.

constructs.label: struct s { int a; char b[4]; };
constructs.note: CONTROL: ordinary struct layout, the C analyzer's core subject.

constructs.label: enum e { A, B = 2, C };
constructs.note: CONTROL: an enumerator with an explicit value and one that continues — the shape the #939 array-dimension fix reads.

verdict.rebaselineNote: The question put to this work was whether a rebuild of the patched source would reproduce the wired bytes, and the answer is that the wired bytes ARE a verified build of the patched source — surface-identical in both directions and behaviourally identical on all 10 constructs — so every C measurement already made against them stands and no re-baseline is required. Had the wired bytes matched pristine upstream instead, the #743b fix would not have been live and the whole lane would have needed re-measuring.
